Hippocampal proteome: ACT vs Sham

Hippocampus proteome (McElroy et al. 2020)

Study design

Hippocampus of 4-month-old female C57BL/6 mice, about four weeks after ACT chemotherapy (doxorubicin + cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel) or sham treatment. Label-free LC-MS/MS quantified with MaxQuant (iBAQ). Data from Table S1 of the supplementary file (ijms-730741) of McElroy et al. (2020), Int. J. Mol. Sci. 21(5):1867, PMID 32182883.

  • Sham: 4 samples.
  • ACT: 4 samples.

Independent re-analysis. Only the raw iBAQ values are used. The authors' normalized values, statistics and protein tables are not used or compared.

Chemotherapy effect only. The study also has MnBuOE and ACT-MnBuOE groups; they are excluded on purpose.

Replicate pair as batch. Replicates 1–2 and 3–4 differ strongly in depth (missing values) in both groups, so the pair is a blocking factor in the model.

Pipeline

  1. prepare (scripts/prepare.sh): extracts annotation + raw iBAQ of the Sham and ACT samples from Table S1 into data/processed.csv.
  2. limma_analysis (scripts/ACT_mcelroy_limma_ijms730741.R): filtering, normalization, imputation, limma, sensitivity analysis without imputation, QC/DE plots, GSEA (GO, KEGG) and ORA.
  3. report (scripts/report.py): this page.

Shared settings:

  • Filter: proteins with ≥ 3 valid (non-zero) iBAQ values in at least one group.
  • Normalization: log2, then median centering per sample.
  • Imputation: left-censored (MinProb-like) draws from N(mean − 1.8 SD, 0.3 SD) per sample, seed 42.
  • limma: ~ 0 + group + batch (batch = replicate pair 1–2 vs 3–4), eBayes(trend = TRUE), contrast ACT − Sham. Positive log2FC = higher in ACT.
  • DE call: FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 0.5; if no protein passes FDR, the unadjusted P < 0.01 is used instead (same fold-change cutoff).
  • GSEA: proteins ranked by sign(log2FC) × −log10(P); GO (BP, CC, MF) and KEGG (mmu) with clusterProfiler, gene sets 10–500, Benjamini-Hochberg, fixed seed. Positive NES = enriched in ACT.
  • ORA: GO BP of the up and down sets against the identified proteome (not the whole genome).

Input data

Input is Table S1 of the supplementary file: one row per MaxQuant protein group, with raw iBAQ intensities per sample. A value of 0 means the protein was not quantified in that sample.

5,514 protein groups are in the table; 5,200 pass the valid-value filter. Replicates 1–2 have many more missing values than replicates 3–4 in both groups.

Quality control

These plots check the data before testing. After median centering the samples should have similar distributions, and replicates of the same group should be close in the PCA.

Intensity distributions

## Densities before / after normalization and imputation
long <- function(m, stage) data.frame(m, check.names = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "sample", values_to = "log2_iBAQ") %>%
  mutate(stage = stage)
dens <- bind_rows(long(log_filt, "1 filtered"), long(log_norm, "2 normalized"),
                  long(log_imp, "3 imputed")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(log2_iBAQ)) %>%
  mutate(group = sub("_.*", "", sample))
p_dens <- ggplot(dens, aes(log2_iBAQ, colour = sample, linetype = group)) +
  geom_density() + facet_wrap(~stage, ncol = 1) + theme_bw()
save_plot(p_dens, "density_preprocessing.pdf", height = 8)

From ACT_mcelroy_limma_ijms730741.R

## Boxplot after normalization (before imputation)
p_box <- long(log_norm, "normalized") %>% filter(!is.na(log2_iBAQ)) %>%
  mutate(group = sub("_.*", "", sample)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(sample, log2_iBAQ, fill = group)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) + theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p_box, "boxplot_normalized.pdf")

From ACT_mcelroy_limma_ijms730741.R

Sample similarity

Replicates 1–2 and 3–4 form two batches (replicate pairs) with very different depth, each with 2 Sham and 2 ACT samples. Without correction the batch is the largest source of variation in the PCA. The limma model estimates it as a term (~ 0 + group + batch); for the plots below the batch is removed with limma::removeBatchEffect (group effect protected), so they show the variation left after the batch.

Variance explained after batch correction: PC1=27.4%, PC2=22.4%, PC3=20.7%, PC4=12%.

## PCA of samples (imputed, batch-corrected matrix)
pca <- prcomp(t(log_bc), scale. = FALSE)
var_expl <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2), 1)
pca_df <- cbind(metadata, pca$x[, 1:3])
p_pca <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group, shape = batch, label = sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) + geom_text_repel(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", var_expl[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", var_expl[2], "%)"),
       title = "PCA, batch-corrected (removeBatchEffect)") +
  theme_bw()
save_plot(p_pca, "pca.pdf")

From ACT_mcelroy_limma_ijms730741.R

Differential abundance

5,200 proteins were tested. 38 proteins pass unadjusted P < 0.01 and |log2FC| > 0.5: 29 up and 9 down in ACT.

No protein passes FDR < 0.05 (0 without the fold-change cutoff), so the unadjusted P < 0.01 is used. These calls are exploratory: with ~5,200 tests, about 52 proteins are expected below P < 0.01 by chance alone.

# Volcano plot: Up = red, Down = blue, NS = gray (same scheme as bulk-rna-seq)
keyvals <- ifelse(tt$status == "Up", "#CC0000", ifelse(tt$status == "Down", "#3399FF", "gray"))
names(keyvals) <- ifelse(keyvals == "#CC0000", "Up", ifelse(keyvals == "#3399FF", "Down", "NS"))
sig_label <- if (sig_col == "adj.P.Val") "FDR" else "P"

p_volc <- EnhancedVolcano(tt,
                          lab = tt$SYMBOL,
                          x = "logFC",
                          y = sig_col,
                          xlab = bquote(~Log[2] ~ "fold change"),
                          ylab = bquote(~-Log[10] ~ .(sig_label)),
                          title = cfg$title,
                          subtitle = "ACT vs Sham",
                          caption = paste("Total proteins:", nrow(tt)),
                          pCutoff = sig_cutoff,
                          FCcutoff = fc_cutoff,
                          pointSize = 1.0,
                          labSize = 3,
                          colCustom = keyvals,
                          colAlpha = 0.5,
                          legendLabSize = 7,
                          legendIconSize = 7,
                          drawConnectors = TRUE,
                          widthConnectors = 0.3,
                          max.overlaps = 15)
save_plot(p_volc, "volcano.pdf", width = 8, height = 7)

## Heatmap of the differentially abundant proteins (batch-corrected, row-scaled)
top_ids <- c(tt_up$Protein, tt_down$Protein)
hm <- log_bc[top_ids, ]
rownames(hm) <- make.unique(tt$SYMBOL[match(top_ids, tt$Protein)])
save_base("heatmap_DE.pdf", width = 6, height = max(5, 0.15 * length(top_ids) + 2), {
  print(pheatmap(hm, scale = "row", cluster_cols = FALSE, silent = TRUE,

                 annotation_colors = list(group = group_colors),
                 main = paste0("DE proteins (", sig_col, " < ", sig_cutoff, "), batch-corrected")))
})

P-value diagnostics

A well-behaved test has a flat p-value histogram with a peak near zero, and a QQ plot that follows the diagonal for most proteins. plotSA shows the intensity-dependent variance trend used by eBayes(trend = TRUE).

## P value / FDR histogram
save_base("pvalue_histogram.pdf", width = 8, height = 4, {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  hist(tt$P.Value, breaks = 50, col = "grey", main = "P value", xlab = "P")
  hist(tt$adj.P.Val, breaks = 50, col = "grey", main = "FDR (BH)", xlab = "adj. P")
})

Sensitivity to imputation

The same limma model was refit on the normalized matrix without imputation (limma skips missing values; proteins absent from a whole group get no estimate). The log2FC with and without imputation correlate with r = 0.655.

20 of 38 DE calls hold without imputation (same direction, same cutoffs). Of the 18 that do not, 4 have no estimate without imputation (missing in a whole group): they are presence/absence patterns rather than quantitative changes, and their large fold changes come mostly from the imputed values.

p_sens <- ggplot(tt, aes(logFC, noimp_logFC, colour = robust_noimp)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey") + geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  geom_text_repel(data = subset(tt, status != "NS"), aes(label = SYMBOL), size = 2.5,
                  max.overlaps = 30, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey50", `TRUE` = "#CC0000")) +
  labs(x = "log2FC (imputed)", y = "log2FC (no imputation)", colour = "DE robust\nwithout imputation") +
  theme_bw()
save_plot(p_sens, "sensitivity_imputation_logFC.pdf", width = 8, height = 7)

Gene set enrichment (GSEA)

GSEA uses all tested proteins, so it also catches pathways where many proteins change a little. This is where the clearest signal of this dataset is, since few single proteins pass the cutoffs.

GO

104 GO terms have padj < 0.05 (79 enriched in ACT, 25 in Sham).

save_plot(dotplot(gse_go, showCategory = 10, split = ".sign") + facet_grid(. ~ .sign),

Over-representation (ORA)

No GO BP term is over-represented in the up (29) or down (9) sets at padj < 0.05: the sets are small compared with the ~5,200-protein background.

Configuration

Show config.yaml
# Parameters for the ACT vs Sham hippocampal proteomics analysis.
# Paths are relative to the project root (proteomics/).

dataset: ijms-730741
title: "Hippocampus proteome (McElroy et al. 2020)"

groups:
  reference: Sham
  treatment: ACT
  colors:
    Sham: "#3399FF"
    ACT: "#CC0000"

data:
  raw_xlsx: data/ijms-730741-SI.xlsx     # supplementary file (Table S1, raw iBAQ)
  processed: data/processed.csv          # output of scripts/prepare.sh, input of the R script

results_dir: results                     # CSV tables
plots_dir: plots                         # PDF + PNG figures
reports_dir: reports                     # report.html and sessionInfo.txt

seed: 42                                 # imputation and GSEA permutations

preprocessing:
  min_valid_per_group: 3                 # keep proteins quantified in >= n replicates of some group
  impute_shift: 1.8                      # MinProb: mean shift (in SD) of the imputation distribution
  impute_width: 0.3                      # MinProb: width (in SD) of the imputation distribution

de:
  fdr_cutoff: 0.05                       # BH FDR, used if any protein passes it
  nominal_cutoff: 0.01                   # unadjusted P, fallback when nothing passes FDR
  logfc_cutoff: 0.5                      # |log2FC|

enrichment:
  min_gs_size: 10
  max_gs_size: 500
  pvalue_cutoff: 0.05                    # BH-adjusted, GSEA and ORA
  run_kegg: true                         # needs internet access to rest.kegg.jp
